Live lab: the value after JWT_SIGNING_KEY= in .env is 64 characters (counted with wc -c, value not printed) = base64 of 48 bytes.

IssuerSigningKey = new SymmetricSecurityKey(Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes(signingKey)) at :38; JwtTokenService.cs:15-16 HmacSha256 on the same setting. claim_verdicts.evidence: Program.cs:23 copies the value into the local `signingKey` before builder.Build(), and TokenValidationParameters is built from that local, so no reload can reach it. docker-compose.yml:92 sets it as an environment variable of the container. r1 live run: the key changed only when the container was recreated. Lesson wording "copies the key once, at startup, from an environment variable" matches.

claim_verdicts.evidence: RFC 8725 sec. 2.2: "Some applications use a keyed Message Authentication Code (MAC) algorithm, such as 'HS256', to sign tokens but supply a weak symmetric key with insufficient entropy (such as a human-memorable password). Such keys are vulnerable to offline brute-force or dictionary attacks once an attacker gets hold of such a token." Forgery by any key holder: Program.cs validates only by recomputing with IssuerSigningKey (plus iss/aud/exp, all readable from a real token); no token store exists in stage-1.
claim_verdicts.source: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8725 sec. 2.2; rfc7518 sec. 3.2; stage-1 Program.cs:22-41

claim_verdicts.evidence: Live run: login -> token; POST /api/v1/orders -> 201. After JWT_SIGNING_KEY=$(openssl rand -base64 48) docker compose up -d api: 502 for ~3 s, then 401 with the same token. After docker compose up -d api: 502 for ~3 s, then 201 (order 35, status new) with the same token. Token lifetime is 8 h (JwtTokenService.cs:28 AddHours(8)), so the restore works only within that window.

Docker docs: "when the same variable is declared by multiple sources, precedence applies: 1. Variables from your shell environment 2. ... --env-file 3. ... .env file". Live output: "Container donhang-api Recreate / Recreated / Starting / Started" for both commands; after the restore the container's key hash equals the .env key hash. App: create_order_screen.dart sets 'Failed: $e' and api_client.dart:55 throws Exception('failed to create order (${response.statusCode})'), so a 401 renders "Failed: Exception: failed to create order (401)".

Follows from claim 4 and the code: OrdersController identity comes from the token's sub, so a forged sub acts as any customer; nothing in Program.cs depends on where the request comes from. RFC 8725 sec. 3.5: "Human-memorizable passwords MUST NOT be directly used as the key to a keyed-MAC algorithm such as 'HS256'."

claim_verdicts.evidence: "In environment variables, a colon separator doesn't work on all platforms. A double underscore (`__`) is supported by all platforms and is automatically converted into a colon (`:`) when the configuration is read by the app." Applies to docker-compose.yml:92 Jwt__SigningKey -> Program.cs:23 Configuration["Jwt:SigningKey"].
